scope: Original text and original positions of every element. Replace three illustrations only.

hero.retouch: Two feathered local colour adjustments derived from mean source/donor colour on original camera pixels. No generative texture composited.

prompts.construction:
Create a photographic diptych for two small side-by-side print pictures for a British vegetable gardening book. One landscape file, fully filled, exactly two equally sized SQUARE independent documentary photographs, clean vertical split dead centre at 50%, no gutter, type, frames, panel labels, effects or overlays. The two show DIFFERENT gardens and two home-made bins MID-CONSTRUCTION. The subjects must read at 32mm print width; show almost the whole main bay in each square including its opening and the context of what is being built. Natural casual garden snapshots, ordinary light, rectilinear camera lens. Good edges without artificial polish.

LEFT square: authentic reconstruction of building the third masonry compost bay in John's small Cornish front garden. Both reference photos are the same real site: reference 1 shows the half-height walls and reference 2 the real third bay with the lintel just built and the EXISTING bay with a weathered plank door to its right. Base this frame faithfully on reference 2. A little wider and slightly higher so we see the complete new bay and the near edge of its right-hand neighbour. A small roughly cubic bay against the existing rough grey boundary wall, low walls made of SMALL reused buff-grey concrete BRICKS in staggered courses. The front has two short sturdy masonry jambs, a wide OPEN doorway and one straight grey concrete lintel on the two jambs. No door or lid installed yet on the new bay. Standing beside it on the right is the earlier bay with its weathered wooden door and felted lid. The one action: a gardener's dusty hand and sleeve entering from upper left is keeping a short straight aluminium spirit level flat on the recently mortared brick course across the lintel. Both ends of the level rest on the course, no floating tools. The hand is peripheral, the structure is the subject. Maybe a small mortar bucket on the earth by the opening. Keep the ground, leaves, slightly wonky repairs, reclaimed mottled brick and modest scale of John's real photo.

RIGHT square: new independent candid photograph in a different modest British kitchen garden, showing construction of a single square wooden compost bin. Designed from common UK working examples of close-boarded walls and removable front boards, not a replica of a published image. An establishing three-quarter view from above waist height shows the side, open front and bare soil floor of ONE bin, the front facing us at a slight angle. Three full-height, close-boarded horizontal walls already screwed to four stout square corner posts. At front, two straight parallel guides capture the ends of the separate front boards. A pair of ordinary adult hands on either end of ONE broad plank guiding it horizontally down the grooves between the two front posts. A few lower front boards already in place with a substantial open area above; both plank ends visibly align with their channels. A simple close-boarded wooden lid with a batten across its underside leans against the side ON THE GROUND, clearly a separate part awaiting fitting, with its edges wholly inside the picture. Use slightly mismatched reused timber in muted grey and honey tones, close joints, warm overcast light, actual irregular turf and earth, quiet blurred hedge. View must show the complete timber box and loose lid. No pallets with gaping openings, no crisscross slats, extra boxes, brand markings or showroom finish. In both pictures the person is cropped to forearms or hands only, never a face.
prompts.spot_retouch: Precision spot-retouch of the supplied real camera photograph. SAME original closely cropped panoramic photograph, same 3:1 frame, all three lids down, every plank and hinge, every weed, the brickwork, the mud, moss, nail holes, knotholes, rusty hasps, mottled grey and green weathering and even the scrap of wood on the central lid retained. Do not redraw, reconstruct, relight or clean the bin as a whole. The weathered original is what we like. There are only two small marks to soften slightly: a small patch of dull green algae partway down one middle plank of the centre door, and a small patch of dark green streaking on one board of the right-hand door. Bring the colour of just those tiny spots a little closer to the surrounding old wood; let all the original grain show through. Preserve all other stain marks, dings, asymmetry, tonal range, black roofing felt and garden clutter. It should take a side-by-side comparison to spot the difference. No other changes.
